scope: Matched protocol bundles: full replacement vs one-slot patch, each with at most one correction. Different schemas/instructions are part of the interface; not a pure wording causal test or H2 learning.

cases.request: Make the pulse in the third move clear. Keep its move name and preserve the first, second, and fourth source moves exactly.
Make the opening hold use the same variation as the final hold. The final hold is already clear, so change only the opening hold; leave the two middle moves and final move unchanged.
Replace the sway in the second slot with a pulse, keeping that slot's variation soft. Preserve the other three approved source moves.
Change the later of the two pulses, the third move, into a sway. Keep its variation soft and leave the earlier pulse and both endpoints exactly as they are.
Only the two middle slots are editable. Leave the earlier middle sway untouched; make the later middle pulse clear. Preserve the rise and settle.

First, change the second-slot sway into a clear pulse. Final correction: do not change that second slot after all; instead make the third-slot pulse soft. The final correction replaces the earlier edit, and all other source moves stay exactly as they were.
Of the two editable endpoints, change the opening hold to soft. Keep the ending settle and both approved middle moves unchanged.
The last move is already a clear hold. Set the move immediately before that hold, the settle, to clear too. Do not change the hold or either earlier source move.

design: Models sequential; condition order alternates by case and reverses by model; same source/request/approved scope. Case oracle stays host-only. No mutation of source or executing motion during model calls.
repair: Compiler rejection supplied; accepted-but-wrong edit gets generic reminder. Experimental oracle triggers retries, not a production prose verifier.
